teams.name: Next Stop
teams.description:
SecureFlow AI is an AI-powered, behavior-based fraud detection system designed to make digital payments safer. It analyzes transactions in real time using factors such as amount, merchant, time, device, location, and transaction history.

A Risk Engine combines rule-based detection, behavioral analysis, and machine learning such as XGBoost to generate a risk score from 0–100. Based on the score, transactions are allowed, flagged for verification, or blocked.

Its key feature is adaptive verification, where suspicious transactions require user confirmation instead of automatic rejection. Graph-based analysis can also identify suspicious relationships between accounts and transactions.

Built as a safe simulation using React/Next.js, FastAPI, Python, XGBoost, and SQLite, SecureFlow AI aims to provide proactive, personalized, and intelligent fraud prevention.

teams.name: SignToStack
teams.description: I'm planning on building SignToStack, which is a VLA pipeline concept that translates spatial American Sign Language gestures directly into production-ready software architecture. Using MediaPipe, the application will track hand landmarks to capture architectural signs, like gesturing a "Sidebar", and compile those spatial intents. IBM Bob 2.0 will then act as an accessibility architect. Rather than just generating basic boilerplate, Bob will use those gestures to dynamically render semantic HTML, inject strict ARIA tags, and configure focus management. My goal is to break the keyboard bottleneck and allow developers to build inclusive web infrastructure purely through physical motion.

teams.name: Cubiczan
teams.description:
Point Bob at any legacy repo and get a health score, renovation plan, and guided modernization — in one click.
The Problem
Every engineering team has that repo — 50k+ lines of undocumented, untested code written 8 years ago in an outdated framework. Nobody wants to touch it, but the business depends on it. Onboarding a new developer takes weeks. Every change risks breaking something invisible. Technical debt compounds silently until a rewrite becomes the only option — and rewrites fail 70% of the time.

The Concept
Developer tool built on top of IBM Bob 2.0's multi-agent orchestration that transforms how teams approach legacy code.

teams.name: Tech Fenatics
teams.description:
AI Design-Debt Reviewer is an automated UI quality checker for developers, operating like a linter but focused entirely on design issues that standard code linters miss.
When modernizing enterprise applications—such as legacy RPG-generated UIs running on IBM i—design reviews are typically manual, slow, and inconsistent, causing critical accessibility and spacing issues to slip through to production.
Powered by IBM Bob in Agent Mode, our tool deploys multiple specialized subagents in parallel to catch design debt instantly before it ships:
* Accessibility Agent: Flags poor color contrast and compliance errors.
* Spacing Agent: Detects layout anomalies and padding inconsistencies.
* Pattern Agent: Catches generic or mismatched boilerplate designs.
By combining deep repo context with line-level accuracy, it provides actionable, direct fixes instead of generic feedback. This fits perfectly into the hackathon’s code review track, reducing cycles and automating design quality at scale.

We're building an AI-powered assistant that helps developers understand and work with unfamiliar codebases faster, using IBM Bob 2.0's full repository context. Our goal is to reduce the time developers spend "getting oriented" in a new codebase, whether they're joining a team project, contributing to open source, or picking up an internship task. By combining Bob 2.0's repository-aware reasoning with a simple, intuitive interface, we aim to make onboarding to any codebase faster, clearer, and less intimidating — especially for students and early-career developers.

teams.name: Techno Giants
teams.description:
ReviewPilot — Subagent-Based Code Review Orchestrator
Code review is a major SDLC bottleneck: reviewers juggle style checks, logic/security risks, and test coverage gaps at once, often missing issues under time pressure. ReviewPilot uses IBM Bob 2.0's subagent architecture to parallelize the review itself. Three subagents run concurrently, each with its own clean context: one audits style and lint compliance, another reasons about logic and security vulnerabilities, and a third checks whether test coverage keeps pace with code changes. A main orchestrating agent merges all three reports into one prioritized review comment, sorted by High/Medium/Low severity. This turns a manual, sequential 10–15 minute review into a fast, repeatable workflow — with nothing slipping through the cracks. Built with Python and Flask as a lightweight orchestration layer around Bob's agent mode, ReviewPilot shows how subagents turn a single-threaded human bottleneck into scalable, automated code review.

teams.name: Lotus
teams.description: Kessler Copilot is an AI-powered space-debris collision-avoidance advisor that transforms raw orbital tracking data into actionable mission-safety insights. It continuously ingests live TLE data for ~25,000 tracked objects, propagates orbits using the industry-standard SGP4 model, and detects future conjunctions threatening satellites or the ISS. Each event receives a quantitative collision-risk score based on miss distance and approach geometry. An agentic LLM layer powered by IBM Granite converts complex orbital mechanics into plain-language risk briefings, recommended avoidance maneuvers, and interactive Q&A. Real-time 3D visualization lets operators, students, and the public understand conjunctions and maneuver decisions. Built end-to-end with IBM Bob, Kessler Copilot makes space situational awareness more accessible, intuitive, and actionable.
